controls.label: Query matrix Q
controls.help: Editing a query row changes that row of the score matrix S, then that row of the attention weight matrix A, and finally that row of the attention output.

controls.label: Key matrix K
controls.help: Editing a key row changes one column of the score matrix S, which reshapes every row of the attention weight matrix A and therefore the attention output.

controls.label: Value matrix V
controls.help: Editing a value row does not change the score matrix S or the weight matrix A, but it changes the attention output, which is the weighted average of these rows.

controls.label: Score gain g
controls.help: Multiplies every score before the softmax; a larger gain sharpens the attention weight matrix A towards a single entry per row, raises the largest attention weight, and pulls the attention output towards one value row.

controls.label: Divide scores by sqrt(d_k)
controls.help: When on, every score is divided by sqrt(2), which shrinks the score matrix S and keeps the attention weight matrix A less concentrated; when off, raw dot products feed the softmax, so g alone controls how peaked A becomes.

explorations.title: Equal keys give a uniform attention row
explorations.instruction: Predict: if all three key rows are identical, what happens to the three weights in each row of A and to the output row? Then apply the preset, which sets the key matrix K to three identical rows and turns scaling on with the score gain at 1.
explorations.observe: Every entry of the attention weight matrix A becomes 0.3333, the largest attention weight readout drops to 0.3333, the row sums of A stay at 1, and each row of the attention output becomes 0.667 and 0.667, the plain average of the three value rows.
explorations.why: Identical key rows give the same dot product with a given query, so all three scores in each row of S are equal; the softmax of equal scores is the uniform distribution 1/3, so A spreads mass evenly, and A V is just the unweighted mean of the value rows.

explorations.title: Removing the scale and boosting the gain concentrates a row
explorations.instruction: Predict: with the sqrt(d_k) division switched off and the score gain raised to 4, do the weights stay balanced or concentrate on one key? Then apply the preset, which turns scaling off and sets the score gain to 4.
explorations.observe: Rows 1 and 2 of A stay near 0.495, 0.0091 and 0.495, row 3 of A becomes about 0.0177, 0.0177 and 0.9647, the largest attention weight readout rises to about 0.9647, and row 3 of the attention output moves to about 0.982 and 0.982, close to value row 3.
explorations.why: Without the division by sqrt(2), multiplying every score by g = 4 widens the gap between the largest and the remaining scores in each row of S; after exponentiating, the largest score dominates the row sum, so that row of A puts almost all its mass on one key and the output row becomes nearly that key's value row.
